**[00:58]** Wherefore I wish you, Nasitas and Aquila, to go before me in two separate bodies and to enter secretly into the Gentile cities. **[32:29]** To this I answered, "Those therefore who do wrong are not guilty because they wrong the just by the judgment of God." Then Peter said, "They indeed sin greatly, for they have given themselves to sin. Wherefore, knowing this, God chooses from among them some to punish those who righteously repented of their former sins, that the evil things done by the just before their repentance may be remitted through this punishment. But to the wicked who punish and desire to exploit them and will not repent, it is permitted to exploit the just for the filling up their of their own punishment. For without the will of Yahweh, not even a sparrow can fall to the into a snare. Thus, even the hairs of the just are numbered by Yahweh. But But he is just who, for the sake of what is reasonable, fights with nature.

**[33:16]** For example, it is natural to all to love those who love them, but the just man tries also to love his enemies and to bless those who slander him and even to pray for his enemies and to compassionate those who do him wrong. Wherefore also, he refrains from doing wrong and blesses those who curse him and pardons those who strike him and submits to those who persecute him and salutes those who do not salute him. Shares such things as he has with those who have not. Persuades him that is angry with him. Conciliates his enemy. Exhorts the disobedient. Instructs the unbelieving. Comforts the mourner. Being distressed, he endures. Being ungratefully treated, he is not angry. But having devoted himself to love his neighbor as himself, he is not afraid of poverty but becomes poor by sharing his possessions with those who have none.

**[34:06]** But neither does he punish the sinner, for he who loves his neighbor as himself, as he knows that when he has sinned, he does not wish to be punished. So, neither does he punish those who sin. And as he wishes to be praised and blessed and honored and to have all his sins forgiven, thus he does to his neighbor loving him as himself. In one word, what he wishes for himself, he wishes also for his neighbor, for this is the law of Yahweh and of the prophets. This is the doctrine of proof of And this perfect love toward every man is the male part of philanthropy, but the female part of it is compassion. That is to feed the hungry, give drink to the thirsty, clothe the naked, visit the sick, take in the stranger, and show herself to and help to the utmost of her power him who is in prison. And in short, have compassion on him who is in misfortune.

**[34:55]** But I hearing this said, "These things indeed it is impossible to do, but to do good to enemies bearing all their insolences, I do not think can possibly be in human nature." Then Peter answered, "You have said truly, for philanthropy being the cause of immortality is given for much." Then I said, "How then is it possible to get it in the mind?" Then Peter answered, "Oh beloved Clement, the way to get it is this. If anyone be persuaded that the enemies ill using for a time those whom they hate become the cause of them of deliverance from the eternal punishment, and forthwith he will ardently love them as benefactors. But the way to get it, oh dear Clement, is but one, which is the fear of God.

**[35:38]** For he who fears God cannot indeed from the first love his neighbor as himself, for such a order does not occur to the soul. But by the fear of God he's able to do the things of those who love, and thus while he does the deeds of love, bride love is it, as it were, brought to the bridegroom fear. And thus this bride being forth philanthropic thoughts makes her possessor immortal as an accurate image of God, which cannot be subject in its nature to corruption. Thus while he expounded to us the doctrine of philanthropy, the evening having set in, we turned to sleep. All right, that's the end of book 12, and we will pick it up next time, book 13.

**[36:21]** Shalom.
